fields.description:
## Symptom

`transition_ticket(fattish-plucky-bufflehead, "in_progress" -> "closed")` over MCP
returned `McpError: -32001: Request timed out` on three successive attempts. The
ticket stayed `in_progress` each time. The call runs the completion-verifier close
gate inline, and that gate takes 9-11 minutes by `AGENTS.md`'s own published
estimate, against an MCP client request deadline of roughly 60 seconds.

The timeout is not a verdict. The server keeps running, the caller learns nothing,
and the natural response is to re-fire the same call -- a second billable gate pass.
This is precisely the failure `AGENTS.md` already describes for the direct gate
tools, and the reason `review_plan_start` / `verify_completion_start` exist.

## Why the existing workaround does not cover it

Pre-computing the attestation does NOT make the close fast. Measured on
`62dc-535b-5d05-421d` at `origin/main` `f1fe7c6f587d3a57fcd4b49598485d7fd4101711`:

1. `verify_completion_start` -> job
   `1793725995508270393-89be127e921a4bf8b7acd1bbfaee7749`.
2. `gate_status` -> `status: "passed"`, `verdict: "PASS"`,
   `verified_at_sha: f1fe7c6f587...`, `signed_at: 1793726842234944794`.
3. `transition_ticket` with that signed certificate in place -> **timed out again**.

So the async surface covers the gate op but not the operation that actually needs
it. An agent that follows the documented guidance still cannot close a ticket over
MCP without an ambiguous timeout.

## Scope: which surfaces run a gate with no async counterpart

In `src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py`, `_start_gate_job` and `_spawn_gate_daemon` are already generic
over `gate_type` -- the daemon machinery is not the gap; only two gates use it:
- `_register_gate_start_tools` registers exactly two starters: `review_plan_start` and
  `verify_completion_start`.
- `_gate_sidecar_fields` hard-restricts `{"plan_review", "verify_completion"}`.
- `rebar/llm/gate_runs.py` (`_durable_verdict`, `_GATE_SIDECARS`), the `gate_status` docstring
  in `_mcp_reads.py`, and `schemas/gate_run.schema.json` describe only those two job kinds.

Surfaces that run one of the long gates inline with NO async form:

| Surface | Gate run inline | Async form |
|---|---|---|
| `transition_ticket` (`_mcp_tool_specs.py`) | completion-verifier on a close (`transition_close.close_ticket`) | none |
| `review_code` (`_mcp_llm.py`) | four-pass code review | none |

Out of the gate-running scope, verified in code: `claim_ticket` and the `open -> in_progress`
branch of `transition_ticket` go through `gates.plan_review_precheck`, which only calls
`llm.claim_gate_check` -- a local HMAC + freshness check with no LLM and no network call
(`_commands/gates.py:319-366`). They return in milliseconds and need no starter. The
`claim --review` flag that does run `llm.review_plan` is CLI-only and not exposed over MCP.

`review_code` is the clearest gap: a long LLM gate op registered synchronously alongside
`review_plan` and `verify_completion`, which both got starters.

## Invariant to establish

Every MCP surface that runs the plan-review, completion-verifier, or code-review gate must
have an async counterpart returning a `{job_id, ..., status: "running"}` handle pollable by
`gate_status`, so no caller is ever forced into a request that can outlive the client
deadline. Today the invariant holds for 2 surfaces (`review_plan`, `verify_completion`) and
fails for 2 (`review_code`, `transition_ticket`).

## Design

- `review_code_start` (in `_mcp_llm.py`) mirrors `review_plan_start`, with gate type
  `code_review`, an empty `ticket_id` (a code review covers a git range), and a dedup variant
  carrying `base`/`head`/`source`. The sync `review_code` and the starter share one body
  (`_review_code_body`) so a provider failure is the same structured result on both, and the
  sync tool goes through `run_gate_singleflight` with the same key.
- `transition_ticket_start` (new `src/rebar/_mcp_ticket_async.py`) wraps the SAME derived
  `transition_ticket` tool (spec pre/post hooks included) and runs it on the gate daemon via
  `_start_gate_job`. It uses its own gate type `transition`, not `verify_completion`: the dedup
  key starts with the gate type, so reusing `verify_completion` would let a close ATTACH to a
  running `verify_completion_start`, report that check's `passed`, and never transition. A
  completed transition settles `passed` with verdict `applied`; a refusal (gate FAIL,
  ConcurrencyError) settles `failed` with the message in `error`. Registered from
  `mcp_server.build_server` and skipped on a read-only server, like the write tools.
- `_terminal_from_result` unwraps the nested code-review verdict dict to its PASS/BLOCK string;
  `_gate_sidecar_fields` reads a `GATE_TYPES_WITH_SIDECARS` constant that includes `code_review`.
- `gate_runs._durable_verdict` maps a `transition` job to the ticket's completion-certificate
  currency, so a close poller sees whether the completion cert persisted.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 -- `review_code_start` exists, returns a `{job_id, ticket_id, gate_type,
  status: "running"}` handle in milliseconds, and its job is pollable through `gate_status` to
  a terminal `passed`/`failed` carrying the review's PASS/BLOCK verdict.
- [ ] AC2 -- `transition_ticket_start` starts the transition (and its completion-verifier close
  gate) on a daemon, returns a handle immediately, and applies the status change only on gate
  success -- so a close over MCP is never blocked on an inline gate run.
- [ ] AC3 -- `gate_status` reports the new `code_review` and `transition` job kinds (gate type,
  verdict, and for `transition` the durable completion currency), and `_gate_sidecar_fields`
  no longer silently drops sidecar provenance for `code_review`. The `gate_status` docstring and
  the `GateRun` schema description name every starter.
- [ ] AC4 -- a test drives each new starter through `gate_status` to a terminal state,
  asserting the handle returned BEFORE the gate completed (a terminal-verdict-only test would
  pass against the blocking code this bug is about).
- [ ] AC5 -- a test asserts the invariant directly against the real `build_server()`: every
  registered MCP tool that runs one of the three gates has a `<name>_start` counterpart, and a
  second test classifies every billable LLM tool so a new gate surface cannot ship without one.
- [ ] AC6 -- `docs/mcp-reference.md` (regenerated by `scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py`, which must
  enumerate the new registrar) documents the new starters, and the `AGENTS.md` async-gate
  guidance that names only `review_plan` / `verify_completion` is widened to every
  gate-running surface.
- [ ] AC7 -- de-dup protection applies to the new surfaces as it does to synchronous
  `review_plan` / `verify_completion`: a re-fire while a run is in flight attaches to it (same
  `job_id`, one gate run) instead of double-billing.

## Provider neutrality

Nothing here is provider- or model-specific. The daemon machinery, job handle, and polling
surface are all transport-level and indifferent to which provider backs a gate.

## Out of scope

- Changing any gate's verdict logic, prompt, or criteria.
- Raising the MCP client request deadline -- a client setting, and it would not fix a
  10-minute gate behind a 60-second deadline anyway.
- CLI surfaces, which are not subject to the MCP request deadline.
